title: Multimodal Engineering
lede: Vision (OCR-via-LLM, document AI), voice (STT/TTS, realtime APIs from OpenAI / LiveKit / Vapi), image generation (Flux, SDXL, Imagen, DALL-E; ControlNet, LoRA, ComfyUI), and video generation (Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling). Each section ships in two voices: the engineer's version (technical, with code & diagrams) and a layman's version (plain English with analogies). প্রতিটি টপিকের শেষে বাংলা ব্যাখ্যাও আছে।

sections.title: Multimodal engineering (vision, voice, video)
sections.sub: Text was the first modality. In 2025, every production AI app combines at least two of vision, voice, image generation, and video generation. Multimodal engineering is the discipline of choosing models, latency budgets, and pipelines for each.

body.html: Vision: image understanding, OCR-via-LLM, document AI
Native multimodal models (GPT-4o, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3-VL) take images directly. The killer use cases:

items: OCR-via-LLM: an LLM beats Tesseract on messy photos, handwritten notes, and structured forms. Often no separate OCR step needed.[28]
Document AI: PDF understanding with layout awareness (Claude, Mistral OCR, Qwen2-VL).
Chart/diagram extraction: ask the model to read a chart and emit JSON.

body.html: Voice agents: STT, TTS, realtime APIs
A voice pipeline is STT → LLM → TTS. Each has its own SOTA:

rows: OpenAI Realtime API, LiveKit Agents, Vapi, Retell, Daily

body.html: Realtime APIs skip the chunky STT→LLM→TTS loop by streaming audio bidirectionally. Sub-500 ms turn-taking is now achievable. LiveKit and Vapi ship full agent frameworks on top of these.[29]

Workflows: ControlNet for structure (pose, depth, canny edges), LoRA for style or character consistency, inpainting for edits, IP-Adapter for reference images. ComfyUI lets you wire these into reproducible pipelines.
ComfyUI, Replicate, Fal for media pipelines

items: ComfyUI — node-based UI for Stable Diffusion / Flux workflows. The "Figma for diffusion." Production teams version-control the JSON graphs.
Replicate — pay-per-second API for any open-source model. The fastest way to deploy something you found on Hugging Face.
Fal — fast hosted inference for diffusion, with streaming partial results.

layman.html: AI isn't just text anymore. In 2025 every serious AI app combines at least two of: looking at images, listening to voice, generating images, generating video. Each has its own model, its own trade-off, and its own best-practice pipeline.

Vision ("AI that sees"): Native multimodal models like GPT-4o, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5 take images directly — no separate OCR step needed. They can read a photo of a receipt, look at a screenshot and tell you what's wrong, extract the data from a chart, or understand a PDF's layout. They beat traditional OCR tools on messy real-world images.

Voice ("AI that hears and talks"): The old way is a 3-step pipeline: speech-to-text → LLM → text-to-speech. Each step adds latency. STT (speech-to-text) tools: Whisper, Deepgram, AssemblyAI. TTS (text-to-speech) tools: ElevenLabs, Cartesia, OpenAI TTS. Realtime APIs (OpenAI Realtime, LiveKit, Vapi) stream audio both directions without the chunky step-by-step loop — the AI interrupts itself, pauses naturally, and feels like a real conversation.

Image generation ("AI that draws"): Flux, SDXL, Imagen, DALL-E — pick by what you need: open weights and fine-tunability (Flux, SDXL), photorealism (Imagen), instruction-following (DALL-E). Advanced: ControlNet lets you say "draw this character in this pose"; LoRA lets you teach it a model in the style you want; inpainting lets you edit part of an image. ComfyUI is the node-based UI where you wire these into reproducible pipelines.

Video generation ("AI that films"): Sora (OpenAI), Veo 3 (Google, with native audio), Kling (Kuaishou, longer), Runway (character continuity), Pika/Luma/Hailuo (cheaper, faster). Most produce 5–20 second clips. Quality is now broadcast-grade for short social-media content.

Production plumbing: Replicate is "give me a credit card and I'll run any open-source AI model for you per second." Fal is the same with speed-optimised diffusion. ComfyUI is the Figma-for-diffusion tool: node-based UI that you can version-control and run headlessly.

blocks.html: The studio analogy: think of an AI studio in 2025. The vision model is the camera operator. The voice model is the dubbing artist. The image-generation model is the illustrator. The video model is the director of photography. ComfyUI is the studio's workflow tool — where you plug the camera, the artist, and the director into one pipeline. Replicate/Fal is "rent a GPU by the hour, no need to buy your own."

bangla.html: এআই আর শুধু টেক্সট নয়। ২০২৫-এ প্রতিটি গুরুতর AI অ্যাপ অন্তত দুটির সমন্বয় করে — চিত্র দেখা, কণ্ঠ শোনা, চিত্র তৈরি, ভিডিও তৈরি। প্রতিটির নিজস্ব মডেল, ট্রেড-অফ ও সেরা-অনুশীলন পাইপলাইন আছে।

Vision ("যে AI দেখে"): GPT-4o, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5 এর মতো নেটিভ multimodal মডেলগুলো সরাসরি চিত্র নেয় — কোনো আলাদা OCR ধাপের দরকার নেই। তারা রসিদের ছবি পড়তে, স্ক্রিনশট দেখে বলতে এটি কী ভুল, চার্ট থেকে ডেটা বের করতে, বা PDF-এর layout বুঝতে পারে। তারা বাস্তব-বিশ্বের অগোছালো চিত্রে ঐতিহ্যবাহী OCR tools-কে ছাড়িয়ে যায়।[28]

Voice ("যে AI শোনে ও কথা বলে"): পুরোনো উপায় হলো ৩-ধাপের pipeline: speech-to-text → LLM → text-to-speech। প্রতিটি ধাপ latency যোগ করে। STT (speech-to-text) tools: Whisper, Deepgram, AssemblyAI। TTS (text-to-speech) tools: ElevenLabs, Cartesia, OpenAI TTS। Realtime APIs (OpenAI Realtime, LiveKit, Vapi) chunky ধাপে-ধাপে লুপ ছাড়াই উভয় দিকে audio stream করে — AI নিজেই নিজেকে interrupt করে, স্বাভাবিকভাবে pause নেয়, এবং আসল কথোপকথনের মতো অনুভূত হয়।[29]

Image generation ("যে AI আঁকে"): Flux, SDXL, Imagen, DALL-E — আপনার প্রয়োজন অনুযায়ী বেছে নিন: open weights ও fine-tunability (Flux, SDXL), photorealism (Imagen), instruction-following (DALL-E)। উন্নত: ControlNet আপনাকে বলতে দেয় "এই চরিত্রটি এই pose-এ আঁক"; LoRA আপনাকে আপনার পছন্দের স্টাইলে শেখায়; inpainting একটি চিত্রের অংশ সম্পাদনা করতে দেয়। ComfyUI হলো node-based UI যেখানে আপনি এগুলো reproducible pipeline-এ সংযুক্ত করেন।

Video generation ("যে AI চিত্রগ্রহণ করে"): Sora (OpenAI), Veo 3 (Google, native audio সহ), Kling (Kuaishou, দীর্ঘ), Runway (চরিত্রের ধারাবাহিকতা), Pika/Luma/Hailuo (সস্তা, দ্রুত)। বেশিরভাগ ৫–২০ সেকেন্ডের ক্লিপ তৈরি করে। স্বল্প social-media কন্টেন্টের জন্য মান এখন broadcast-grade।

Production plumbing: Replicate হলো "আমাকে একটি ক্রেডিট কার্ড দাও এবং আমি যেকোনো open-source AI মডেল প্রতি সেকেন্ডে চালাব।" Fal একই কিন্তু speed-optimised diffusion। ComfyUI হলো diffusion-এর জন্য Figma: node-based UI যা version-control ও headless চালানো যায়।

blocks.html: স্টুডিওর উপমা: ২০২৫-এর AI স্টুডিও ভাবুন। Vision মডেল হলো camera operator। Voice মডেল হলো dubbing artist। Image-generation মডেল হলো illustrator। Video মডেল হলো director of photography। ComfyUI হলো স্টুডিওর workflow tool — যেখানে camera, artist ও director-কে একটি pipeline-এ প্লাগ করা হয়। Replicate/Fal হলো "নিজের GPU না কিনে ঘণ্টা ভাড়ায় ভাড়া নাও।"

practice.title: Extract JSON from a messy photo
practice.goal: See that a multimodal model can read messy text in an image and return structured data, and that it can still guess wrong.
steps: Pick any everyday photo or screenshot with text: a receipt, a sign, a menu, or a handwritten note. Cover private data first.
Attach the image in a new chat and send Prompt A. Take a photo with your phone if you have none.
No image upload in your chat? Send Prompt B instead. It has a typed sample of a blurry receipt.
Compare each JSON value with the real image or sample. Mark every value that is wrong or guessed.
Read the unclear list. Did the model say what it could not read?

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
Look at the attached image.
Step 1: Write all the text you can read, in order.
Step 2: Return JSON with these keys:
- item_type (for example receipt, sign, menu, note)
- title (the main heading, or null)
- dates (list)
- numbers (list of every number you can read, as written)
- unclear (list of parts you could not read well)
Do not guess. If a part is hard to read, put it in unclear and do not put it in the other keys.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
Below is the text that came from a blurry photo of a shop receipt. Some characters are wrong.

---
RAHIM GR0CERY STOR3
12 Moy 2O25
Rice 5kg ....... 4SO
Oil 1L ......... 18O
Eggs (12) ...... ??5
Total .......... 8l5
---

Return JSON with these keys:
- item_type
- title
- dates (list)
- numbers (list of every number, as written)
- unclear (list of parts you could not read well)
Do not guess. If a part is hard to read, put it in unclear and do not put it in the other keys.

lookFor: Most models read messy or handwritten text well, with no separate OCR tool.
Some values may be wrong, or the model may fix a broken character without telling you.
A model that follows the rule puts hard parts in unclear. The explicit do not guess rule changes this a lot.
The JSON is easy for a program to read. The free text of Step 1 is not.

check.question: Why is asking for JSON with an unclear field better than just asking the model to read the image?
check.answer: OCR-via-LLM turns an image into structured data in one step, but the model can guess wrong. The JSON gives a program a fixed shape, and the unclear field makes the model report doubt so you can check those parts by hand.

practice.challenge: Send Prompt A again with a worse image, for example a dark or tilted photo. Which keys break first?

practice.title: Ask better questions about a screenshot
practice.goal: See that a precise visual question gives a far more useful answer than a vague one.
steps: Take a screenshot of any app or web page you use, such as a form or a settings screen. Hide private data.
Attach it in a new chat and send Prompt A. Save the answer.
Attach the same image in another new chat and send Prompt B. Compare the two answers.
No image upload? Send Prompt C in one new chat. Then send only its first paragraph plus What do you think? in another new chat.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text: What do you think of this image?

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
This is a screenshot of an app screen.
1. Say in one sentence what the screen is for.
2. List up to 3 things that look wrong or confusing, such as cut-off text, low contrast, or unclear buttons. For each one, say where it is on the screen.
3. List what you cannot judge from this image.
Be specific. Do not praise the design.

prompts.label: Prompt C
prompts.text:
Here is a description of a screenshot, because I cannot upload it.
The screen is a checkout page for a phone shop. At the top, a title says "Pay" in light grey on a white background. In the middle, a field named "Phone numbr" has a red border but no message. At the bottom, two buttons sit next to each other: a big green button with the text "OK" and a small grey button with the text "Cancel". The price "BDT 12,4" is cut off at the right edge.

1. Say in one sentence what the screen is for.
2. List up to 3 things that look wrong or confusing. For each one, say where it is on the screen.
3. List what you cannot judge from this description.
Be specific. Do not praise the design.

lookFor: Prompt A usually gives a general, polite answer about colours and mood.
Prompt B gives located, testable problems, such as a cut-off number or a weak button label.
Most models list some limits in item 3, for example that they cannot see how the screen behaves when you tap it.
Visual Q&A works best when you say what to look for.

check.question: Why does Prompt B give a more useful answer than Prompt A, when the image is the same?
check.answer: Visual Q&A is still a prompt. The model needs a task, a format, and a limit on what to report. A vague question leaves it free to describe the image, but a precise question makes it find problems.

practice.challenge: Ask the model to return the three problems as JSON with the keys problem, location, and severity.

practice.title: Find the slow stage in a voice agent
practice.goal: See how each stage of an STT, LLM, and TTS pipeline adds delay, and why realtime audio helps.
steps: Read the numbers in Prompt A. Write your own guess of the total delay and of the slowest stage before you send it.
Send Prompt A in a new chat. Compare the answer with your guess.
In the same chat, send Prompt B to compare with a realtime design.
Pick one change from the answer that costs the least work. Say why you chose it.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
I build a voice agent for a bank help line. The design is speech-to-text (STT), then an LLM, then text-to-speech (TTS). After the caller stops talking, the delays are:
- Wait to be sure the caller finished speaking: 600 ms
- STT finishes the final text: 400 ms
- LLM sends its first token: 700 ms
- The system waits for the LLM to finish a full sentence before it sends text to TTS: 300 ms
- TTS makes the first audio: 350 ms
- Network to the caller: 150 ms

1. Add up the total delay before the caller hears the first sound.
2. Name the stage that is the biggest and the stage that is the easiest to cut.
3. Suggest two changes. For each, say how many ms it might save and what could go wrong.
Use a small table.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
Now my team thinks about a realtime audio API. Audio streams in both directions, and the model starts to speak after about 450 ms in total.
1. Which stages of my old design disappear?
2. Give me two things I might lose, for example control, logging, or the choice of voice.
3. Give me one rule to decide between the two designs for a bank help line.
Answer in 8 lines or fewer.

lookFor: The total is 2,500 ms. Check the model added it correctly.
Every stage waits for the one before it, so small delays add up.
Good suggestions often stream LLM tokens into TTS, and shorten the end-of-speech wait.
Most models say that a realtime API gives up some control over each stage.

check.question: Why is a pipeline of STT, LLM, and TTS slower than a realtime audio API?
check.answer: In a pipeline, each stage waits for the previous stage to finish, so the delays add up. A realtime API streams audio in both directions, which removes the waits and makes fast turn-taking, under about 500 ms, possible.

practice.challenge: Change one number in Prompt A, for example make the LLM 1,500 ms. Ask which change now saves the most time.

practice.title: Choose tools for image generation jobs
practice.goal: Learn which image generation tool fits which job: ControlNet, LoRA, inpainting, or IP-Adapter.
steps: Read the four jobs in Prompt A. Write your own choice for each job on paper first.
Send Prompt A in a new chat. Mark each job where the model and you disagree.
In the same chat, send Prompt B. Check whether the pipeline matches the job.
If your chat can make images, ask it to draw job 3 and see if it can edit only one part.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
I use a diffusion image pipeline. These tools exist: ControlNet (structure such as pose, depth, or edges), LoRA (a small trained add-on for a style or a character), inpainting (edit one masked area), and IP-Adapter (use a reference image as a guide).

For each job, pick the best tool, give one reason, and say what input I must have.
Job 1: Make 20 posters with the same cartoon girl in the same drawing style.
Job 2: Keep the exact pose of a person in my photo, but turn the photo into a painting.
Job 3: Change only the sky in a product photo and leave the product as it is.
Job 4: Make a new picture that has the colours and mood of one reference image, with no training.
If two tools could work, say so.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text: Take Job 2 and write the pipeline as a numbered list of nodes, as in ComfyUI. For each node, write its name, its input, and its output. Then give two reasons why a team should keep the pipeline as a saved graph file in version control.

lookFor: Most models pick ControlNet for Job 2, inpainting for Job 3, and IP-Adapter for Job 4.
Job 1 may get LoRA, or IP-Adapter, or both. The model should explain the difference.
In Prompt B each node takes the output of a node before it, like a chain.
A saved graph can be reviewed, repeated, and rolled back, like code.

check.question: What is the difference between ControlNet and LoRA?
check.answer: ControlNet controls the structure of one image, such as a pose or edges, from an input you give each time. A LoRA is a small trained add-on that teaches the model a style or a character, so it can repeat them in many images.

practice.challenge: Add Job 5: put a person from a photo into a new background without changing the face. Ask which tools you need and in what order.
